build: Birzzle Fever iOS 1.0.4 with ASLR-relative request, failure, NSError, and privacy-filtered API/host hooks
operator_observation: After a few seconds of loading animation, the same dialog appeared: Failed to connect to network. Please check network status.
interpretation: Request ID 1 used the captured hostname and failed DNS resolution in this session. The API hook emitted a fixed privacy fallback instead of an uppercase dotted command: this does not establish its actual API or reply contract. The archived Objective-C request bridge creates an NSString with format %s from a caller-supplied native C string; static code does not reveal the runtime argument here. Historical Android offline response files have a matching iOS file crypto key, but their local lookup and iOS routing remain unverified. No offline iOS save or replacement server was installed.
next_action: Map the native request API's runtime value through a privacy-safe exact-command matcher or static callsite evidence after a separate manual readiness gate. Establish native save root, identity selection, and actual iOS response lookup before bootstrapping the historical Android identity into an iOS offline save.
privacy: No token, member identifier, UDID, account data, full URL, request parameters, or crash filename is included. Raw syslog stays private in ignored ios/captures. Android was not used.
